chunks: That the pilgrim and the one performing Umrah return like two newborns: one of them died as an infant, with no sin upon him, and the other lived for as long as he lived protected from sin.

key_terms.الْحَاجَّ: the person performing hajj, the major pilgrimage
key_terms.الْمُعْتَمِرَ: the person performing Umrah, the lesser pilgrimage
key_terms.طِفْلًا: an infant, one who has not reached moral responsibility
key_terms.كَمَوْلُودَيْنِ: like two newborns, indicating complete purity from sin
key_terms.مَعْصُومًا: protected from sin; here indicating sinlessness in the comparison
key_terms.يَرْجِعَانِ: they return, meaning they come back spiritually transformed

ai.seo_question: How does hajj or Umrah affect a person's sins according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration describes the spiritual effect of hajj and Umrah as a return to a state of purity and freedom from sin. It emphasizes the immense grace associated with these acts of worship and the cleansing they bring to the believer.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: "The pilgrim and the one performing Umrah return like two newborns—one who died as an infant without sin, and the other who lived their life free from sin."
